#en: Been picking through this dead node so long I can taste oxidized metal in my teeth. Most of the consoles here are ghosts, but one of the cores still had heat left in it, tucked behind a wall panel someone thought was welded shut. Jump data, tightened and cleaned in a way no company mechanic around here could dream of, all bent around the same kink in the lanes we have been chasing. Whoever pulled that Fleet package knew exactly what they were stealing; half these coordinates match the accidents everybody swears were just bad luck. The funny part is, the route strings keep referencing a salvage yard on Deimos, like the path always folds back through there before it disappears. I have heard that place mentioned in bar talk for months, always as a joke, always with eyes dropping to the floor the second anyone asks for details.
zh: 我在这座死节点里翻拣得太久，牙缝里都尝得到氧化金属的味道。这里的控制台大多是鬼影，可其中一个核心还留着余温，藏在某块被人以为焊死了的墙板后面。跃迁数据被收紧、清洗过，手法是这一带任何公司技工都想象不出来的，全都绕着我们一直在追的那处航道扭结弯折。把那份舰队数据包拽出来的人，清楚自己在偷什么；这些坐标有一半对得上人人都赌咒说只是运气不好的那些事故。好笑的是，航路串一再提到火卫二上的一座打捞场，仿佛那条路径在消失前总要从那儿折返一次。这地方我在酒吧闲谈里听人提过好几个月了，每次都是当笑话讲，每次一有人问细节，所有人的眼睛就齐刷刷落到地上。

#en: They started changing the duty roster about a year back, but it did not feel like anything at the time. Different pilots pairing with different convoys, a few routes shuffled off the public boards, the usual corporate "optimization" spin. I remember one morning at the TerraBrew stall near Dock 17, seeing a Vanguard jacket at a table that never hosted uniforms before, talking low with a Ryujin type who smelled like fresh plastic and old secrets. Nobody cared. Ships came and went, GalBank still paid out, LIST settlers still limped through bad systems with just enough fuel and just enough luck. Only later, when the same name started whispering through Neon bars and insurance disputes, did it hit me that all those small adjustments were drawing lines around one pilot, setting her apart from the rest of us without ever saying why.
zh: 大约一年前，他们开始改动值班表，但那会儿谁也没觉得有什么。不同的飞行员配不同的运输队，几条航线从公示板上撤下，照例是那套企业式的"优化"说辞。我记得有天早上，在 17 号泊位附近的地球酿酒摊位上，看见一件先锋队夹克坐在从不接待制服客的桌旁，压低声音跟一个闻起来像新塑料与旧秘密的龙神家伙说话。没人在意。飞船来了又走，银河银行照常付款，独立盟的定居者仍靠着刚好够的燃料和刚好够的运气，一瘸一拐地穿过糟糕的星系。直到后来，同一个名字开始在霓虹城的酒吧和保险纠纷里低语，我才猛然意识到：所有那些小小的调整，都在围着一名飞行员画线，把她从我们其余人里单独圈出来，却从不说为什么。

#en: I keep telling myself I am only here because the pay is good, that I do not care why some Aegis ghost bled out on this rock with their datapad hugged to their chest. But I walked the perimeter twice before I even cracked the casing. No sign of a fight, no distress beacon in the logs, just a gap in the record where a human being should have left noise. That bothers me more than any scorch mark would have.  \n\nThe file fragments mention a safety inspector who stopped filing reports, a freighter that never finished its jump, and a research contract whose number does not exist in the public registries. Nothing links on paper. Names change, timestamps drift, routes get reclassified. Every time I think I see the chain of events, it smears sideways, like the universe is refusing to hold still long enough for anyone to write it down.
zh: 我不断告诉自己，我来这儿只是因为报酬不错，我根本不在乎某个神盾的鬼为什么胸口紧抱着数据板，流干了血死在这块岩石上。可在我撬开外壳之前，我先绕着外围走了两圈。没有任何打斗的痕迹，日志里也没有求救信标，只有记录中一段空白——一个活人本该在那里留下声响。这比任何焦痕都更让我不安。\n\n文件碎片里提到一名不再提交报告的安全检查员、一艘从未完成跃迁的货船，以及一份编号在公开登记册里查不到的研究合同。纸面上什么都串不起来。名字会变，时间戳会漂，航线会被重新归类。每次我以为自己看清了事件的链条，它就朝侧面糊开一片，仿佛宇宙不肯为任何人的记录静止得足够久。

#en: They say some places in space hold on to things longer than they should. The microgravity platform I swung past today is one of them. It should be scrap and silence, just another drilling rig left to spin itself apart, but the patrol grid still flinches every time its old transponder breathes. I parked just outside the lane and listened; there is a thin, dirty signal riding the standard telemetry, nudging any tagged-for-disposal hull a few degrees off its proper course. Every dock rat back on the station "knows" to give this sector a wide berth, then suddenly forgets why when you press them. Between the dead spacer's slate and that corrupted buoy I burned, both pointing at misrouted wrecks and retired codes that refuse to die, it feels like this whole patch of sky is hanging onto someone else's mistakes until they can be quietly erased.
zh: 都说太空里有些地方比它们该有的样子更念旧。我今天绕过去的那座微重力平台就是其中之一。它本该只剩废铁与寂静，不过又一座任其自行转散的钻井平台，可它的老应答器每喘一口气，巡逻网格就会缩一下。我停在航道外侧听着；有一道又细又脏的信号骑着标准遥测，把任何被打上"待处置"标签的船壳推开几度，偏离它们正确的航向。空间站上每个码头老鼠都"知道"该绕开这片区域，可你一追问，他们又突然忘了为什么。从那个死去太空人的数据板，到我烧掉的那只损坏浮标，两者都指向被错引的残骸和拒绝死去的退役代码——感觉这一整片天空都攥着别人的错误不放，直到它们能被悄悄抹去。

#en: I am parked off this ore platform, watching it turn like it has for decades, still humming through a pattern nobody bothered to erase. Somewhere along the way, some clerk signed the wrong form or looked the other way, and that tiny shrug of bureaucracy carved out a blind lane in the sky. Now the platform's guidance is stitched into bar gossip and half-lost sensor logs, echoes of the same freighter silhouette skimming grids where no one should be. I keep thinking about that first dead homestead, the dirty telemetry from its orbit, the way local fauna started acting like they got new orders. None of it screamed conspiracy at the time. Just glitches. Just bad luck. But all those small, quiet mistakes and compromises nudged things toward this forgotten dot on the map, until everything strange seems to lean, just a little, in this direction.
zh: 我停在这座矿石平台外侧，看着它像几十年来那样旋转，仍在嗡嗡作响地走着一套没人费心去抹除的图案。一路上，某个文员签错了表格，或是别过头去，而官僚系统那一下微不足道的耸肩，就在天上凿出了一条盲航道。如今这平台的导航已缝进了酒吧闲谈和半遗失的传感器日志里，回响着同一个货船轮廓掠过本不该有人的网格。我总想起第一座死去的农庄、它轨道上传来的肮脏遥测，还有当地动物开始像接到新命令一样行事。当时这些都没什么阴谋的味道。只是故障。只是运气不好。可所有那些小小的、安静的失误与妥协，把一切都往地图上这个被遗忘的点推去，直到所有古怪的事似乎都稍稍朝这个方向倾斜。

#en: Hard to tell where the real story starts, so I will pin it to that rusted relay I was paid to wake up last month. The work order called it routine: clear a backlog, reset a few buffers, bill some faceless office in New Atlantis. When I got there, half the panels were already scorched, and the logs did not read like simple neglect. Distress calls came in clean, went out smeared, registry tags folded over themselves. Some entries had been sliced and pasted so many times the timestamps looped. A tug crew swears they saw a hijacked signal bouncing through there weeks before; a dockhand insists those same ship IDs showed up later on a private auction list. None of their stories match perfectly, but every broken piece points at the same thing: someone very patient, nudging ghosts through forgotten circuits until the records forgot they were ever alive.
zh: 很难说真正的故事从哪里开始，那就把它钉在上个月有人付钱让我去唤醒的那座锈蚀中继站上吧。工单上说是例行公事：清理积压、重置几个缓冲区、向新亚特兰蒂斯某个不露面的办公室开账单。等我到那里时，一半的面板已经烧焦，日志读起来也不像单纯的疏于维护。求救呼叫进来时清晰，出去时却糊成一片，登记标签自我折叠。有些条目被剪切粘贴了太多次，时间戳都成了死循环。一支拖船船员赌咒说，几周前他们见过被劫持的信号在那里弹来弹去；一名码头工则坚称，同样的船号后来出现在一份私人拍卖清单上。他们的说法没有一条完全吻合，可每一块碎片都指向同一件事：某个极有耐心的人，把幽灵们从被遗忘的电路里拨弄过去，直到记录忘了它们曾经活过。

#en:
Been running cargo runs since before the Armistice, and I have never seen a ship fly itself like the Boneclaw did last week.

We were three days out, grav drive on cooldown, when the nav console lit up with a route I did not punch in.

Looked official, too, buried under old UC formatting nobody bothers with anymore.

Captain swore it was a relic subroutine, some legacy safety corridor from back when the war made everyone jumpy.

Crew laughed it off, let the autopilot ride it, because who argues with a path that clean.

Thing is, the more I dug into the logs after shift, the more I found those same corrections, repeating like a heartbeat, on runs years apart.

Different captains, different cargo, same quiet nudge.

Somewhere out there, something we forgot to shut down is still talking to our ships, and I do not think it is doing us any favors.
zh:
停战之前我就在跑货了，可我从没见过哪艘船像上周的骨爪那样自己飞。

我们已经出航三天，重力驱动在冷却，这时导航控制台亮起一条我没输入过的航线。

看起来还挺正式，埋在如今谁都不屑一用的联殖旧格式下面。

船长赌咒说那是个遗留子程序，战时人人都神经紧绷的年代留下的某种安全走廊。

船员们一笑而过，让自动驾驶顺着它跑，谁会跟一条那么干净的路径较劲呢。

问题是，交班后我越翻日志，就越发现那些相同的修正，像心跳一样重复着，出现在相隔数年的航次里。

不同的船长，不同的货物，同样安静的轻推。

在外面的某处，某个我们忘了关掉的东西仍在跟我们的飞船说话，而我不觉得它是在帮我们的忙。

#en: I was supposed to be on a six-month temp contract up here, the kind of nowhere posting you take when you want to disappear without quitting. The module hums and breathes like any other relic on the corporate leash, but the logs feel wrong under my hands. Years of clean mirrored transfers, then suddenly one chain fractures: inbound packets split, some land where they are supposed to, others slip sideways into dead space. The anomalies are tiny, like someone with surgeon hands nudged the code, trusting the redundancy to hide the cut. I flagged it in the maintenance queue, marked for a senior tech to review, and then nothing happened. No follow-up, no purge, just my ticket quietly closed without comment. The gaps stayed in the archive, hanging there like half-erased handwriting, as if whoever was meant to come back and tidy the mess simply never made it this far.
zh: 我本来到这里只是签一份六个月的临时合同，就是那种你在想不辞职就消失时会接的、鸟不拉屎的差事。这个模块像企业牵引绳上任何一件遗物那样嗡鸣、呼吸，可日志在我手底下感觉不对劲。多年的干净镜像传输，然后某一天，一条链突然断裂：入站数据包被劈开，有些落在该落的地方，另一些则侧滑进死寂空间。那些异常极其细微，像有人用外科医生的手拨了拨代码，赌定冗余机制会把切痕藏住。我在维护队列里标记了它，注明要交给资深技师复核，然后什么都没有发生。没有跟进，没有清除，我的工单只是悄无声息地无评语结案。那些缺口留在档案里，像写了一半又被擦掉的字迹悬在那儿，仿佛那个本该回来收拾残局的人，根本没走到这一步。

#en: I was a kid when the first version of the story did the rounds, so I only have thirds and fourths by now. The ones who were there do not agree on much anymore. Some swear the sky over the fields tore open, others say it was just a freighter that came in too hot and shook itself apart. The only constant is that the official report never lined up with what people remember, and every retelling drops another hard detail and picks up another maybe. By the time I was old enough to fly, it was just a warning: do not trust the lanes just because they are lit.\n\nNow there is a new name attached to the old unease, a navigator who walked out on the big flags, a whisper about trials buried in some staryard server. Funny thing is, no one here can tell you exactly when he appeared in the tale; it is like he was always part of it, waiting in the gaps where the truth got rubbed smooth.
zh: 这故事最早流传的时候我还是个孩子，所以如今到我这儿，剩下的已经只是第三手、第四手了。当年在场的人如今也没多少说法能对得上。有人赌咒说田野上方的天空裂开了，另一些人说那不过是一艘进得太急、把自己震散的货船。唯一不变的是：官方报告从来和人们记得的对不上，而每一次转述都会丢掉一个硬邦邦的细节，又添上一个"也许"。等我大到能飞的时候，它已经只剩一句警告：不要因为航道亮着就相信它们。\n\n如今，那份旧日的不安又挂上了一个新名字——一名撇下那些大旗出走的领航员，一句关于埋在某个造船厂服务器里的试验的低语。好笑的是，这里没人说得清他究竟是什么时候进了这个故事；就像他一直在其中，守在真相被磨平的那些缺口里。

#en:
I keep thinking someone is coming back.

The garage is loud enough that no one hears the hum from the old core, not really. Fans rattling, music leaking from a busted speaker, arguments over parts prices. But every time I walk past that one bay, the air feels thinner. Bench wiped spotless in a sea of grime, wrappers folded into a neat little pile, like somebody packed up in a hurry and promised themselves they would finish the job later.

The kid they pulled off the floor swears he blacked out, woke up with his arm set better than UC ever did it. Others say he tripped, patched himself, end of story. Except the med stock sheet does not match, and the Static Hackers keep glancing at that core like it is rigged to bite. If there is a ghost in those logs, it is waiting on the same thing I am: the one who cut here, cleaned here, and walked away before the erase cycle finished.
zh:
我总觉得有人会回来。

车库太吵，没人听得见那台旧核心的嗡鸣，其实根本听不见。风扇嘎吱作响，破喇叭里漏出音乐，还有人为零件价格争吵。可我每次走过那个隔间，空气都显得更稀薄。工作台在一片油污中被擦得一尘不染，包装纸被叠成整整齐齐的一小摞，像是有人匆匆收拾了行装，并向自己保证改天再来收尾。

他们从地上抬走的那个小子赌咒说自己昏了过去，醒来时胳膊被接得比联殖哪次都接得好。别的人说他是自己摔了，自己包扎了，故事到此为止。只是药品库存表对不上，而那帮静电黑客老是瞟着那台核心，像它随时会咬人。如果那些日志里真有个鬼，那它等的和我等的是同一样东西：那个在这里切割、在这里清理、并在擦除周期跑完之前就走掉的人。

#en: Found the packet in the last place anyone checks the old relay's maintenance queue. No alarms, no lockouts, just a half finished transfer flagged "deferred" three years running, sitting in a forgotten subdirectory like somebody fully intended to come back and scrub it clean, then got reassigned or spaced. Atmospheric sweeps layered over patrol routes, with one ship path threaded right through the gaps every time. Same vector, same speed, same little pauses in burn where a careful pilot checks their own work. I pulled the trace forward one more hop and the endpoints start clustering around a junk field that is not on any public navchart, but shows up in system grav noise like a bad memory. First it was that stray record out on the rock, then the cut patterns in the Deimos yard, now this: all of it saying the same thing he has a favorite graveyard, and he keeps going back to it.
zh: 我是在大家最不会去查的地方找到那个数据包的——老中继站的维护队列里。没有警报，没有锁定，只有一次三年来一直被标为"延迟"的半成品传输，躺在一个被遗忘的子目录里，像是某人完全打算回来把它清干净，结果却被调走了，或者被丢进了太空。大气扫描图层叠在巡逻航线上，每次都有一条飞船路径从缝隙中笔直穿过。同样的矢量，同样的速度，同样在点火中那些小小的停顿——那是一个谨慎的飞行员在核对自己的活儿。我把追踪又往前推进了一跳，端点开始聚拢在一片垃圾场上，那地方不在任何公开导航图上，却像一段糟糕的记忆一样出现在星系重力噪声里。先是岩石上那条游离的记录，然后是火卫二船坞里的切割图案，现在又加上这个：全都在说同一件事——他有一处偏爱的墓地，而且他总在回去。

#en: I am logging this from the old drop can, sitting under a flickering strip that should have burned out a decade ago. The place hums with half-dead fans and forgotten protocols; I swear I heard a decon cycle spin up on its own two hours after I powered the generator, like some buried routine still thinks infantry are due in from orbit. That is what got me looking deeper. Under the rust and bootleg wiring, the shelter's systems were still filing traffic, still mirroring route updates to a secondary endpoint nobody bothered to wipe from the registry. Buried in a nav cache I pulled off the liaison's terminal was a repeating destination tag hardwired into his latest corridor updates, same code cross-referenced three times in the old system handshakes. All point toward a relay node tucked in the undergrid of Neon, exactly where no honest captain wants their beacon to light up: Ebbside.
zh: 我在从旧空投舱里记录这段话，头顶是一条十年前就该烧断的闪烁灯带。这地方在半死的风扇和被遗忘的协议间嗡鸣；我发誓在我给发电机供电两小时后，听到了一个净化循环自己转了起来，像某个被埋起来的程序还以为步兵要从轨道上降落。就是那东西让我往深处查了下去。在锈迹与私接线路之下，这座掩体的系统仍在归档交通，仍把航线更新镜像到某个没人费心从登记表里抹去的次级端点。在我从联络员终端上提取的导航缓存里，埋着一个反复出现的目的地标签，硬写进了他最新那批走廊更新中，同一个代码在旧系统握手记录里被交叉引用了三次。全都指向嵌入霓虹城下层电网的一座中继节点——正是任何正派船长都不愿让自己信标亮起的地方：埃布赛德。
